object_description: floating ring of private spaces above seven autonomous ground buildings
design_condition: The ground-level buildings are arranged within the surrounding wall to form differentiated outdoor interstices, while the elevated ring gathers the private spaces above the wall with an unobstructed relationship to the distant plain.

positive.statement: The cross-sectional distribution between the ground world and the upper world is an inventive and clever response to the complex program.
The arrangement generates multiple differentiated spaces for workshops, sport, and well-being.
The upper crown gives all cells an equal and unobstructed relationship with the distant horizon.
The vertical assembly relates coherently to the historic buildings in scale and hierarchy.
The ground-level architecture allows inmates to identify with their division.

negative.statement: The conflict between inmate and delivery flows is real throughout the site.
The underground connection has no natural light and lengthens vertical routes, making management difficult.
The underground position does not comply with the provisions concerning management of the water table.
The long horizontal circuit requires segmentation by grids or doors and will be disrupted by the inevitable cutoff in the first stage.
The structural effort required to support the ring is contradictory with the systematic vertical openings of each cell and requires further study.
The contrast between the two constructive languages underlines the tension or difficulty of supporting the floating ring.
